# dependencytrack Provider

Terraform provider for [OWASP Dependency-Track](https://dependencytrack.org/). It supports both Dependency-Track v4 (tested against 4.14.x, until its upstream end-of-life in December 2026) and v5 (tested against the latest minor, currently 5.2); end-of-life Dependency-Track versions get best-effort support only. At configure time the provider queries the unauthenticated `GET /api/version` endpoint to detect the server's major version and automatically adapts version-dependent behavior (for example, notification publisher identifiers and the deprecated project `author` field); there is no version attribute to set. If that probe fails, provider configuration fails with an actionable error instead of silently guessing a version. Authenticate with exactly one of: an `api_key`, a `username`/`password` pair, or a `workload_identity` block (Dependency-Track 5.2+).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# API Key Authentication
provider "dependencytrack" {
  endpoint = "https://dtrack.example.com"
  api_key  = "your-api-key-here"
}

# Username/Password Authentication
provider "dependencytrack" {
  endpoint = "https://dtrack.example.com"
  username = "admin"
  password = "admin123"
}

# Workload identity federation (Dependency-Track 5.2+): exchange a workload's
# identity token, here a GitHub Actions OIDC token, for a session of a
# service account. See dependencytrack_workload_identity_binding.
provider "dependencytrack" {
  endpoint = "https://dtrack.example.com"

  workload_identity = {
    provider_name   = "github-actions"
    service_account = "ci-pipeline"
    token           = var.github_oidc_token
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `endpoint` (String) The URL of the Dependency-Track server (e.g., https://dtrack.example.com)

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) API key for authenticating with Dependency-Track. Conflicts with username/password authentication.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password for authenticating with Dependency-Track. Must be used with username. Conflicts with api_key authentication.
- `username` (String) Username for authenticating with Dependency-Track. Must be used with password. Conflicts with api_key authentication.
- `workload_identity` (Attributes) Authenticate as a service account through workload identity federation (Dependency-Track 5.2+): the provider exchanges a workload's identity token, such as a GitHub Actions OIDC token, for a Dependency-Track session at configure time. The service account needs a `dependencytrack_workload_identity_binding` that matches the token. The session lasts the workload identity provider's `session_lifetime_seconds` (1 hour by default) and is not refreshed, so a run that takes longer fails once it expires. Conflicts with `api_key` and `username`/`password`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_identity))

<a id="nestedatt--workload_identity"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workload_identity`

Required:

- `provider_name` (String) The name of the Dependency-Track workload identity provider that issued `token`
- `service_account` (String) The name of the service account to authenticate as (without the `svc:` prefix)
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The workload's identity token (a JWT). Read it from a file with `file()` if the platform provides one
